body:
Found 2026-08-09 while answering the SPA web-reader rebuild's data-model questions. Full context:
workspace `notes/KOBO-ANNOTATIONS-WRITEBACK-INVESTIGATION-2026-08-09.md`.

The Kobo device sends `clientLastModifiedUtc` on every annotation in its PATCH body. We DECLARE it
(`cps/readingservices.py:335`, in the `KoboAnnotation` TypedDict) and never read it.
`_upsert_annotation` stamps `last_synced` with server receipt time instead
(`cps/services/annotation_sync/__init__.py:191-193`).

Consequence: **two devices editing the same annotation are ordered by whichever happened to sync
second, not by when the user actually made the edit.** Last-write-wins conflict resolution cannot
be implemented from what we persist. A device that was offline for a week and syncs after a device
that edited yesterday wins.

This is squarely at odds with the stated goal for the annotation subsystem — "so that we have
source of truth and sync correctly" — and it matters more now that the SPA web reader is being
rebuilt around highlights/notes, giving a second authoring surface whose edits must be ordered
against the device's.

Also declared-but-dropped in the same TypedDict, lower stakes: `type` (note vs highlight) and
`location.span.chapterTitle`.

**This is an INGEST bug, not a schema bug.** No migration is implied — the fix is to read the field
and store it, which needs a column decision (reuse vs add) that should go through the sessions
owning `ub.py`. Deliberately not fixed here: the investigation that found it was research-only and
gated against touching the schema or the Kobo sync path.

Related: `annotation_portable.py` already carries `last_synced` in the portable payload, so the
KOReader plugin's diff logic inherits the same ordering weakness.
title: Device clientLastModifiedUtc dropped on ingest — cross-device conflict resolution not implementable
